summary_paragraph: Ms. ___ was admitted with shortness of breath and bright red blood per rectum. She has a complex history including asthma, COPD, prior lung and throat cancer, and chronic steroid use. Her dyspnea was attributed to post-influenza bronchitis and exacerbation of chronic lung disease, with CT showing progression of ground-glass opacities. Bronchoscopy revealed atypical squamous cells and abundant yeast, but no active infection; mucus plugging was cleared. She was started on Bactrim for PCP prophylaxis and received IV immunoglobulin for low IgG, suggesting possible CVID. Hemorrhoidal bleeding was confirmed by anoscopy with stable hemoglobin. Lisinopril was briefly started for hypertension but discontinued due to acute kidney injury. She improved clinically, was weaned off supplemental oxygen, and discharged home with home health, new medications including Spiriva and fexofenadine, and plans for outpatient follow-up with labs, imaging, and specialist visits.
